title: Journal v2: schema-validated, indexed, replayable event log
summary: The journal module is split into five files and grows from a single append-only buffer into a validated event store. Events now carry a typed actor (harness/person/system), an optional work item and change, and a cost; every event is checked against a JSON Schema before a byte is written, and a run-complete event must name the current chain head and closes the run. Journals move from `<state>/buffer` to `<state>/runs`, and the first event of a run with a work item records that run in a per-work-item index file guarded by an advisory file lock. A new reader replays a run, verifying every link, and computes a second digest — the replay digest — over decision fields only, so two runs with identical decisions match even when timings, cache outcomes, cost and run ids differ.

nodes.label: Checkpoint runner
nodes.subtitle: osf verify --checkpoint
nodes.summary: Runs moon tasks for a checkpoint and writes one verification event per task plus a checkpoint-complete event. Now builds an `Actor::system("osf")` and fills the new `check_type`, `summary` and typed `EvidenceGrade` fields.

nodes.label: Review run
nodes.subtitle: review_run.rs
nodes.summary: Writes review-answer and review-decision events. Updated to pass an `Actor` value rather than a bare actor string.

nodes.label: Journal writer
nodes.subtitle: Journal::append / append_draft
nodes.summary: Computes the chain hash, validates the serialised event against the schema, refuses a run-complete whose head hash is not the current head, records the run in the work-item index before the first line, and refuses any event after run-complete.

nodes.label: Event model
nodes.subtitle: event.rs
nodes.summary: The envelope and every payload: actor kinds, cost, evidence grades, work item states, blocked causes, run outcomes, and the ten event types including run-started, review, finding, state-change, run-complete and attention.

nodes.label: Event schema
nodes.subtitle: event.schema.json
nodes.summary: Draft 2020-12 schema for one event, with per-event-type payload branches and cross-field rules: a harness actor must name a model, a blocked state change must carry a cause, and only observed findings may name a verifier.

nodes.label: Schema validator
nodes.subtitle: schema.rs
nodes.summary: Compiles the event schema once per process and validates each serialised event, returning one reason per problem with its JSON path.

nodes.label: Hash chain
nodes.subtitle: hash.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical JSON hashed into each event's SHA-256 link, and the replay digest over decision lines only, which drops timings, cache, cost, run ids and transcripts.

nodes.label: Run index
nodes.subtitle: index.rs
nodes.summary: One JSON file per work item, named by the SHA-256 of the work item id, listing that item's run ids in recorded order. Writes go through a temporary file renamed over the target, under an advisory file lock with a ten-second wait.

nodes.label: Journal reader
nodes.subtitle: reader.rs
nodes.summary: Reads a run back, checking each line's schema, run id, previous hash and recomputed hash before returning anything, and reports the head hash, the replay digest and whether the run completed.

nodes.label: runs/
nodes.subtitle: <state_dir>/runs/<run>.jsonl
nodes.summary: The journal file per run, moved from `buffer/` to `runs/`. Each run is its own hash chain starting from genesis, and a run id is refused unless it is a safe single path component.

nodes.label: index/
nodes.subtitle: <state_dir>/index/<sha256>.json
nodes.summary: Per-work-item run lists, plus a `.lock` file beside each index that serialises concurrent writers.

nodes.label: CI evidence upload
nodes.subtitle: checkpoint-evidence artifact
nodes.summary: The workflow now uploads `$OSF_STATE_DIR/runs` instead of `$OSF_STATE_DIR/buffer`, so the artifact carries the journal files under their new name.

nodes.label: Replay consumer
nodes.subtitle: read_run
nodes.summary: Any caller that replays a run: it gets the events, the head hash that proves the journal is intact, and the replay digest that proves the decisions reproduced.

edges.label: validate(event)
edges.summary: Every event is validated before any byte is written; an invalid event leaves the file and the chain head untouched.

edges.label: record_run(work_item, run)
edges.summary: The first accepted event of a run with a work item records the run in that item's index before the journal line lands, so a failed index update writes no line.

flows.title: Appending one validated event
flows.summary: What happens between a caller handing over a payload and a line landing in the run's journal file, including the index write that must succeed first.

messages.label: append_draft(EventDraft)
messages.note: The draft carries the actor, timestamp, optional cost and payload; the journal supplies the run, work item, change, previous hash and hash.

messages.label: event_hash(prev_hash, payload, actor, cost)
messages.note: The chain hash covers the payload, work item, change, actor and cost, but not the run id or the timestamp.

messages.label: validate(serialised event)
messages.note: A run-complete event is additionally checked against the journal's current head hash.

messages.label: record_run(work_item, run)
messages.note: Only on the first accepted event of a run that names a work item; a failure here refuses the event before any line is written.

messages.label: one JSON line
messages.note: Appended to <state_dir>/runs/<run>.jsonl; the chain head advances only after the write succeeds.

flows.title: Replaying a run and proving it reproduced
flows.summary: The reader checks every line and every link, then reports two hashes: the chain head that proves the journal is intact, and the replay digest that proves the decisions reproduced.

messages.label: validate(line)
messages.note: A schema-invalid line is reported as invalid even when its hash is correct.

messages.label: recompute event_hash and compare
messages.note: A changed duration, cache outcome, payload or deleted line breaks the chain at its own line number.

messages.label: ReplayDigest over decision lines
messages.note: Drops timestamps, durations, cache, cost, run ids and transcripts, so two runs with identical decisions share a digest while their chain heads differ.

views.title: Journal architecture
views.summary: Callers append through the journal writer, which validates against the event schema, chains the hash, records the run in the work-item index and writes a line under runs/. The reader replays the same files and returns both hashes.

children.title: Journal module internals
children.summary: The five files the journal module was split into, and how the writer and reader share the schema, hash and index pieces.

views.title: Append and replay
views.summary: The two ordered sequences this change is about: writing one validated event, and reading a run back to prove it reproduced.
